identity.title: Asymmetric V-shaped amplification-enhanced and PAM-relaxed one-tube dual-mode CRISPR/Cas12a platform for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of foodborne pathogens.

content.abstract: Foodborne pathogen infections pose a serious threat to food safety and public health. As a low-cost method with strong potential for widespread use in most laboratories, conventional PCR and integrated PCR-CRISPR assays are still constrained by prolonged assay times, dedicated instrumentation, limited closed-tube naked-eye visualization, tube-opening-associated contamination risks, and PAM-dependent target recognition, thereby restricting their practical applicability. To address these challenges, we developed an asymmetric V-shaped (rapid thermal cycling) amplification-enhanced CRISPR/Cas12a one-tube dual-mode detection platform. Asymmetric amplification enabled rapid ssDNA enrichment by tuning primer concentrations, reducing amplification time from  approximately 1 h to <30 min while enhancing Cas12a cleavage efficiency and reducing dependence on canonical PAM sites. Moreover, one-tube dual-mode highly sensitive visual pathogen detection (naked-eye: 10 CFU/mL, fluorescence excitation: 1 CFU/mL) was achieved simply by adjusting the probe concentration in the reaction system. By eliminating post-amplification tube opening and reagent transfer while avoiding reliance on nanomaterials or lateral-flow strips, this platform provides a one-tube strategy for rapid, sensitive, and simplified visual detection of foodborne pathogens in resource-limited laboratories.
